title: Scalar contractible tests detect the regular-module open unit
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme and $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme. Let $\Lambda$ be an arbitrary commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with $\Lambda_Z=p_Z^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on each small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Suppose the actual derived restriction $R\Gamma(V,\Lambda_V[0])\to R\Gamma(U\times_XV,\Lambda_{U\times_XV}[0])$ is an isomorphism for every affine weakly contractible $V\to X$ on the full $X$ site [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. Then for every weakly etale $a:Y\to X$ and $j:U\times_XY\to Y$, the specified ordinary unbounded derived adjunction unit [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] $\Lambda_Y[0]\to Rj_*Lj^*\Lambda_Y[0]$ is an isomorphism in the derived category of internal $\Lambda_Y$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], where $\Lambda_Y$ is its regular module. There is no lisse-module assertion; $Y$ need not be affine. Empty schemes and identity opens are included.

proof.text: For j:U times_X Y -> Y, resolve j^*R[0] by a K-injective I. The chain map eta followed by j_* of the resolution represents the exact-left/K-injective-right derived unit. Transport along the canonical exact/K-flat comparison, whose transpose is the identity, to identify it with the specified unit.

proof.text: Regard every Y-site object as an X-site object by composition with a. Cover it on the full X site by affine weakly contractible objects, retaining the maps to Y. Thus every testing object satisfies precisely hscalar on X, with no assertion that its open puncture is weakly contractible.

proof.text: On such a V the evaluated chain map sends x to its restriction on U times_X V followed by the resolution. Restriction of I remains K-injective. The module/abelian derived-sections comparison and exact evaluation on V identify this very arrow with the scalar restriction in hscalar, using naturality; hence it is invertible.

proof.text: The cone evaluates to an acyclic complex on the contractible covering basis. Exact evaluation commutes with cohomology. Sheaf separatedness forces every cohomology sheaf to vanish on all objects; hence the cone is acyclic. Localization inverts the unit, and the exact operations equivalence transports back. This includes empty bases and identity opens.

lean.statement:
theorem isIso_regular_open_unit_of_scalar_tests
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (hscalar : ∀ (V : X.ProEt), IsAffine V.left →
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).IsWeaklyContractible.{u + 1} V →
      IsIso ((Functor.rightDerivedFunctorNatTrans
        ((sheafSections (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}).map
          (show Scheme.ProEt.mk (pullback.snd U.ι V.hom ≫ V.hom) ⟶ V from
            MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (pullback.snd U.ι V.hom) rfl).op)).app
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (condensedRingObj Λ X))))
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (a : Y ⟶ X) [WeaklyEtale a] :
    IsIso ((CondensedRing.derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction Λ
      (pullback.snd U.ι a)).unit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (Mod.regular (condensedRingObj Λ Y))))
